summary: Configured sudo command logging on node1 to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a validated /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging drop-in (Defaults logfile=..., log_year, log_host, !syslog), which records user, host, timestamp, and full command for every sudo invocation while suppressing sudo's syslog/authpriv output so entries never reach /var/log/secure or journald. Verified with both root and a disposable test user. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, issued a background-acknowledged systemctl reboot, confirmed the node went unreachable then came back with a new boot_id, and confirmed the sudoers config, log file, and exclusion from the general system log all survived and continued working post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (AlmaLinux 9.6) and sudo build config (syslog+authpriv logging enabled by default)
Authored /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-command-logging with logfile, log_year/log_host, and !syslog directives; validated with visudo -cf before and after install
Installed the drop-in with mode 0440 and created /var/log/sudo-commands.log with mode 0600 owned by root
Verified logged entries include user, host, timestamp, and command for both root and a temporary non-root sudoer (testsudo), then cleaned up the test user and its sudoers grant
Confirmed no corresponding entries appear in /var/log/secure or journald for the same commands
Captured baseline boot_id and healthy config state, triggered a background-acknowledged systemctl reboot, polled until node1 was reachable again, and confirmed boot_id changed
Post-reboot: re-validated sudoers, confirmed log file and permissions persisted, ran a new sudo command and confirmed it was captured in the log and absent from journald

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
evidence.summary: Created and validated the sudoers drop-in and log file, then showed log entries with timestamp, user (root and testsudo), host, and full command for multiple sudo invocations.

evidence.requirement: Entries kept out of the general system log
evidence.summary: grep against /var/log/secure and journalctl for the logged commands returned zero matches, both before and after the reboot, confirming sudo's syslog output was suppressed via !syslog.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (f43afa1c-4877-4ace-a101-d6bb0cd6ce3d), validated sudoers, and confirmed the log file was populated and correctly permissioned.
systemctl reboot was launched via a backgrounded sleep+reboot wrapper so the exec call returned successfully (pid captured) before the node dropped.

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection timeout) immediately after reboot, then returned with a new boot_id (8c353e7c-f12f-4af6-8a18-9da9f178b5b5), distinct from the baseline, proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging and continued exclusion from general log
evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers config re-validated OK, log file and permissions persisted, a new sudo whoami command was correctly appended to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and journalctl showed zero matching entries for it.
